title: Un-pin / condense the sticky toolbar on mobile
description:
styles.css:56 sets .view-toolbar { position: sticky; top: 0 }. Measured 547px tall at 412px wide = 60% of a 915px viewport and ~70% of a real Pixel 10's ~780px visible area. Confirmed pinning at top:0 across scrollY 400-1200, i.e. the entire range where any view is on screen. Usable height below it is 368px measured, ~233px on device - less than the 278px height of a single .view. The app's only content cannot fit on screen.

It stacks, vertically, at 412px: legend (3 items), 5 layer chips wrapping to 3 ragged right-aligned rows (105px), 2 pill switches + Undo/Redo, month label+slider+readout, scale label+slider+number input, and a 3-bar 'Scale reference' card with a hint line.
design:
Options:
- Drop position:sticky below ~960px, or keep only a ~56px condensed bar (month scrubber + a 'Controls' button) pinned and move the rest into a bottom sheet / <details> drawer.
- The month slider is the core interaction and the one control worth permanent space. Scale, layers, labels, lock, undo/redo and the legend are set-once-then-forget.
- Move the legend and 'Scale reference' card below the views or into the drawer.
- Collapse the scale row: #scaleInput duplicates #scaleSlider, and each view already renders its own '1 ft = N px' badge (.view-scale).
acceptance_criteria: At 412x915, a complete .view is visible on screen at the same time as whatever toolbar remains pinned.
close_reason: view-toolbar drops position:sticky below 960px, verified in 412x915 iframe

title: Tap a plant to open a species detail sheet
description:
On mobile there is no way to see species details by touch. Provable from source; a resized desktop browser has hover and will falsely appear to work.

- Details are delivered ONLY through native SVG <title> tooltips (src/render/tooltip.js -> renderTopView / renderElevationView). Confirmed 192 <title> elements for 192 plant groups. <title> never fires on touch.
- styles.css reinforces this with '.view svg [data-name]:hover { cursor: pointer }'.
- Species table cross-highlighting is bound to mouseenter/mouseleave (src/app.js:734-735) - hover-only.
- Clone is bound to contextmenu (src/app.js:522), and a document click handler at :541 hides the menu. Android long-press over SVG should be verified on-device rather than assumed, but there is no discoverable tap affordance either way.

Net: tapping a plant on a phone does nothing. The species table at the bottom of a 7-screen page is the only route to details and is disconnected from the plant you tapped.
design:
Add a click/pointerup handler on [data-plant-id] that opens a bottom sheet rendering buildTooltipLines(plant, state), plus a 'Clone' action - this reuses the existing tooltip builder and replaces the contextmenu-only clone path with something that works on both input types. Mirror mouseenter/mouseleave on species rows with click-to-pin highlighting. Keep the <title> elements: they remain the desktop tooltip and the accessible name.

Blast radius (codegraph impact buildTooltipLines): tooltip.js, topView.js, elevationViews.js, renderViews.js, tests/topView.test.js, tests/elevationViews.test.js.
acceptance_criteria: Tapping a plant in any of the three views opens a detail sheet with the same content the desktop tooltip shows, and offers Clone. No regression to the existing <title> tooltips.
close_reason: tap [data-plant-id] opens a bottom detail sheet (buildTooltipLines content) with a Clone action; verified via headless iframe at 412x915, existing SVG <title> tooltips unaffected

title: touch-action:none while unlocked swallows page scroll over every view
description:
src/interaction/dragController.js:170 and :349 set svg.style.touchAction = locked ? 'auto' : 'none'. Verified: with positions unlocked, all three view SVGs compute touch-action:none.

Each view is 370x278 inside a 412px column, so any vertical swipe that STARTS on a drawing is swallowed and the page will not scroll. With three views stacked, most of the scrollable area is dead. This is the single most maddening mobile behavior in the app, and is half the reason the scrolling feels 'nested'.

Locked is the default (lockToggle checked, no localStorage on first visit), so a first-time visitor will not hit this - but it makes editing on a phone effectively impossible.
design:
Either:
- use touch-action: pan-y instead of none while unlocked, so vertical page scroll survives and drags read as horizontal/hold gestures; or
- require a long-press (or tap-to-select-then-drag) to begin a touch drag, keeping touch-action:auto until that gesture is recognized.

Blast radius (codegraph impact createPlantDragController): dragController.js, src/app.js init.
acceptance_criteria: With positions unlocked on a touch device, a vertical swipe starting on a drawing scrolls the page, and dragging a plant still works.
close_reason: touch-action: pan-y instead of none, preserves vertical page scroll while unlocked

title: 'Maximize' is a no-op below 960px
description:
Clicking [data-maximize-target="topView"] at 412px leaves the view at exactly 370x278 - unchanged, measured before and after.

Cause: the max-width:960px breakpoint already sets .views { grid-template-columns: 1fr } (styles.css:905), so hiding the other two panels frees no width, and .view { aspect-ratio: var(--view-aspect-ratio, 4/3) } locks height to width. A tall phone cannot trade its width for height.

Three 'Maximize' buttons therefore occupy header space on mobile and deliver nothing.
design:
Options:
- On mobile make maximize mean full-viewport: position:fixed; inset:0 with aspect-ratio:auto, letting the SVG letterbox. The SVG already carries preserveAspectRatio='xMidYMid meet' (src/render/viewConfig.js), so this is mostly CSS.
- Or replace the three stacked panels with a swipeable/tabbed single view (Plan | South | East) so one drawing gets the whole column instead of a third of a 7-screen page.
- Add pinch-to-zoom / pan inside a maximized view: at 370px wide a 30ft yard renders plants a few pixels across and the species initials are unreadable.
acceptance_criteria: On a phone, maximizing a view makes it meaningfully larger than 370x278.
close_reason: maximized view goes position:fixed inset:0 with aspect-ratio:auto below 960px, verified view expands to fill viewport

title: Mobile UX overhaul (Pixel 10 class, ~412px viewport)
description:
The app is close to unusable on a phone. Measured in a 412x915 viewport against 'node server.js':

- Sticky .view-toolbar is 547px tall = 60% of a 915px viewport, ~70% of a real Pixel 10's ~780px visible area. It pins at top:0 for the whole scroll range where any drawing is on screen, leaving ~233px on device vs a 278px .view height. You cannot see one complete drawing while it is pinned.
- No tap path to species details exists at all (SVG <title> is hover-only).
- touch-action:none while unlocked swallows vertical scroll over every drawing.
- 'Maximize' is a no-op below 960px.
- Only one media query exists (max-width:960px); nothing targets phone width.
- Document is 6450px ~= 7 screens; 4615px of that is the species table.

No nested scroll containers and no horizontal overflow were found at 412px - the 'nested scroll' feeling comes from the pinned toolbar plus touch-action:none, not from a scroll container.

Full review with measurements: see child issues; each carries its own numbers.
design: Findings 2 and 3 (touch input) were argued from source, not browser automation: automated clicks are pointerType 'mouse' and a resized desktop window still has hover, so a browser check would have falsely shown them as working. Findings 1, 4, 5, 6 are browser-measured.
close_reason: All 7 mobile UX findings addressed: toolbar un-pinned, tap-to-detail sheet, touch scroll fixed, Maximize works below 960px, phone breakpoint added with clean chip wrapping, header trimmed + species cards collapsible, and tap-target/resize/scale-input polish. Verified via iframe testing at 412px and 1400px.

title: Project-scoped persistence endpoints
description: Scope /api/layout, /api/history, and /api/history/cursor to a project, resolving projects/<slug>/planting_layout.csv and layout-history.json. Validate the slug shape and confirm resolved paths stay inside the projects directory, since a client-supplied id now feeds a file path.
acceptance_criteria: Endpoints read/write the correct project files; traversal attempts and malformed slugs are rejected with 400; omitting the project falls back to the default.

title: Make viewBox, offsets, and backgrounds per-project
description: Thread per-project viewBox dimensions and elevation offsets through configureViews, topView, elevationViews, and the bundle export instead of reading module-level constants. Move the hard-coded background URLs out of styles.css and app.js VIEW_BACKGROUNDS so they come from project config.
acceptance_criteria: No renderer reads PLAN_VIEWBOX/ELEVATION_VIEWBOX directly for geometry; constants remain only as defaults; backgrounds are applied from project config.

title: Compass-direction elevation views
description: Generalize renderSouthElevation/renderEastElevation into one renderer driven by the compass direction the viewer stands on (north/south/east/west), deriving the horizontal yard axis, whether it is mirrored, and the front-to-back depth ordering. View labels come from project config instead of hard-coded index.html text, and the elevation drag controllers use the project-derived axis.
acceptance_criteria: Viewing from south/east reproduces today's output exactly; viewing from north/west mirrors the horizontal axis and reverses depth ordering; labels reflect config.

title: Project config schema, loader, and on-disk migration
description: Add projects/index.json + projects/<slug>/project.json, a src/data/projectConfig.js loader that normalizes and validates config, and migrate the existing yard into projects/backyard/ (planting_layout.csv + img/).
acceptance_criteria: projectConfig parses and normalizes a config with defaults; invalid slugs and missing fields are rejected; existing backyard renders unchanged from its new location.

title: Support multiple projects
description: Allow the app to host several landscape projects, each with its own background images, canvas dimensions, and compass orientation for the elevation views. plants.csv stays a shared global species catalog; each project has its own planting_layout.csv so its species selection is implicitly separate. Projects are authored on disk (projects/<slug>/) and chosen in-app via a picker that navigates to ?project=<slug>.
design: On-disk convention: projects/index.json lists projects; projects/<slug>/project.json declares viewBoxes, background images, default scale, and the compass direction each elevation is viewed from; projects/<slug>/planting_layout.csv holds placements; projects/<slug>/img/ holds backgrounds. Switching projects reloads the page with ?project=<slug> rather than re-initializing app state in place. Yard axes: origin SW, x increases east, y increases north.

title: Add a real phone breakpoint and fix the ragged layer chips
description: styles.css has exactly ONE media query: max-width:960px. Below it, .view-toolbar__actions and .view-toolbar__control-group both keep min-width:280px (styles.css:82 and :91). At ~388px of content width two 280px boxes cannot share a row, so they wrap and stack. Confirmed no overflow results, but it is why the 5 layer chips land in three ragged right-aligned rows (105px tall).
design:
- Add a max-width:600px (or 640px) breakpoint for genuine phone layout.
- Below it, drop the min-width:280px floors and switch justify-content:flex-end / align-items:flex-end to stretch or flex-start, so chips form a clean full-width wrap or a horizontal scroller instead of ragged right-alignment.
- The 5 layer chips are 5 mutually-exclusive states of ONE setting - that is a segmented control or a <select>, not 5 buttons. Their long labels ('Hide trees + sculptural', 'Hide through accents') are also what forces the wrapping.
close_reason: Added max-width:600px breakpoint; dropped the 280px min-width floors on toolbar actions/control-group; chips now flex into a clean 2-col grid instead of ragged right-aligned rows. Verified via iframe at 412px.

title: Trim the header and collapse species cards
description:
The document is 6450px at 412px wide, about 7 screens.

- .page-header is 170px of the first screen and includes a .data-note paragraph about serving CSVs with 'npx serve' - developer instructions occupying ~20% of a phone's first screen.
- .species-table is 4615px: 12 species x ~385px, because the <=960px card layout renders all 10 columns as labelled rows per species.
design:
- Hide .data-note on mobile, or move it into the error-banner path, which is the only time it is actionable.
- Shrink h1 from 1.6rem; consider folding the project picker into the same condensed bar as the month scrubber.
- Make species cards collapsible: label + common name + botanical name by default, with height/width/growth form/sun/water/soil/bloom behind a <details> disclosure. That takes the block from ~4615px to roughly 900px.
- Once the tap-a-plant sheet exists, the species table becomes a browse surface rather than the only detail surface, and can be a compact list.
close_reason: Hid dev-only .data-note and shrank h1 to 1.15rem on phone (<=600px). Species cards now default to label+botanical+common name with a per-row 'Details' toggle revealing height/width/growth-form/sun/water/soil/bloom; table height for 12 species dropped from ~4615px to ~2061px collapsed. Desktop table (>960px) unchanged - verified 10 columns, toggle cell display:none, in a 1400px iframe.

title: Add Playwright end-to-end browser tests
description: No automated browser tests exist; tests/ is all node --test unit tests with a fake DOM. Add Playwright e2e specs that boot server.js and assert on rendered SVG DOM (not screenshots) so agents need not drive Chrome manually.

title: Remove four-nerve daisies from backyard layout
description: Two four-nerve-daisy-front rows in projects/backyard/planting_layout.csv should be deleted.

title: Tests and docs for multi-project support
description: Cover project config parsing, compass-direction elevation geometry, and server project path resolution. Update tests/persistence.test.cjs for the project-scoped URL, and update AGENTS.md (mirrored into CLAUDE.md) for the new on-disk layout.
acceptance_criteria: npm test passes; AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md describe projects/ and how to add a project.

title: Project picker UI and ?project= routing
description: Add a project selector to the header that navigates to ?project=<slug>; app.js resolves the active project from the query string, falling back to the default in projects/index.json.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a project reloads into that project; an unknown or missing slug falls back to the default with a visible notice.

title: Mobile polish: tap targets, resize thrash, numeric scale input
description:
Smaller items from the mobile review.

- Tap targets below the 44px guideline: chips 31px tall, #projectSelect 29px, .view-panel__toggle ~24px. Pill switches at 46px are fine.
- window.addEventListener('resize', render) (src/app.js:520): Android's address bar showing/hiding and the keyboard opening on #scaleInput both fire resize, causing a full re-render of 192 plant groups x 3 views mid-scroll. Debounce it, or compare dimensions before re-rendering.
- #scaleInput is type='number' with step='0.01' - opens a numeric keypad and is fiddly on touch. On mobile the slider alone (plus the per-view '1 ft = N px' badge) is enough.

NOT a problem, checked and confirmed fine: the drag hitbox. MIN_HITBOX_RADIUS_PX = 28 (dragController.js:3) is multiplied by scaleFactor = viewBox / rect (:362, :418), so it is 28 SCREEN px regardless of render size. No small-screen inversion; a 56px-diameter target is acceptable.
close_reason: Tap targets (chips, view-panel__toggle, projectSelect) bumped to 44px min-height on phone (<=600px). Resize handler debounced 150ms and skips re-render when innerWidth is unchanged, so address-bar show/hide and keyboard-open no longer force a full 192-group x3-view re-render. #scaleInput (numeric keypad) hidden on phone; slider + per-view badge remain. Verified in-browser at 412px.

title: Layout history seeds bypass parsePlantLayoutCsv validation
description: appState.plants can come from layoutHistoryInstance.getCurrentPlants() (src/app.js), which is seeded from the server's layout-history.json. Those entries are plain plant arrays and never pass through parsePlantLayoutCsv, so the duplicate-id constraint added in nl-92d does not cover them. Not reachable today: cloning routes through buildCloneId, CSV load now throws, and a scan of projects/example-frontyard/layout-history.json (6 entries) found no duplicates. Worth closing if a future path writes history directly.
acceptance_criteria: Either history seeds are validated on load, or a note records why the path is safe by construction.

title: Duplicate plant id in backyard planting_layout.csv
description: projects/backyard/planting_layout.csv has two rows sharing the id 'four-nerve-daisy-front' (lines 26 and 27). Ids are used to look up plants for dragging, cloning, and hover/target highlighting, so the second row is effectively unreachable — dragging either silhouette moves the first match. Pre-existing, found while verifying the multi-project change; not caused by it.
acceptance_criteria: Every id in planting_layout.csv is unique; consider validating uniqueness in parsePlantLayoutCsv.
close_reason: Duplicates already removed by nl-y8y; parsePlantLayoutCsv now throws on repeated ids, with unit tests.
